11117: No literal infringement because the accused camera mount is not a book holder and is not secured by removable attachment.

We conclude that substantial evidence supports the jury's verdict of infringement of claims 1 and 7 of the '301 patent, claim 1 of the '262 patent, and claim 1 of the '374 patent.
11557: Literal infringement: accused features cannot in isolation unlock data mode, so summary judgment of noninfringement was warranted.

11575: Literal infringement: summary judgment of noninfringement of the '913 and '022 patents affirmed, with Moskowitz conceding non-infringement under the court's construction of 'universal'.
we affirm its grant of summary judgment of noninfringement as to those patents.
11576: Literal infringement of claim 1 of the '319 patent ('cooperating' limitation): denial of JMOL of infringement affirmed because substantial evidence supported the jury's finding of noninfringement.

11584: Summary judgment of noninfringement of claims 1 and 5 of the '430 patent (emulation limitation); court affirmed.

11646: Literal infringement: denial of new trial on infringement of non-Qualcomm-chip Samsung devices; jury verdict of noninfringement left in place under abuse-of-discretion review.

11931: Literal infringement: summary judgment of noninfringement because accused Freestyle dispensers do not literally meet the ordered-step limitation.

12002: Literal infringement: summary judgment of non-infringement affirmed because LTC failed to raise a genuine dispute that MV2's panels meet the 'resisting' limitation

12023: Literal infringement: summary judgment that the Accused Products do not meet the supercontinuum white light pulse limitation, affirmed because it rests on the adopted claim construction.

12433: Literal infringement: the Apple Watch was found to infringe the asserted claims.

12484: Literal infringement: whether substantial evidence supports jury finding that accused SureForm products meet the 'configured to cause' limitation of claim 6

12551: Noninfringement of claim 11 (and 12, 13, 15) of the '180 patent under the 'configured to' limitation; summary judgment of noninfringement affirmed
the district court did not err in finding that the Accused Products do not meet the "configured to" limitation.
12553: Noninfringement of claims 13, 14 and 15 of the '324 patent under the 'sandwiched' limitation; affirmed

12555: Noninfringement of the 'three spaced apertures' limitation of claims 17, 19, 20, 23 and 25 of the '324 patent; affirmed

12684: Literal infringement of claim 9 of the '497 patent and claim 1 of the '253 patent: summary judgment of noninfringement affirmed because the relied-on structure for the rendering function was inadequate.

12829: Literal infringement of the '802 patent by Nexus's ANDA product, affirmed

13078: Design patent infringement likelihood of success: district court found no likelihood that the accused handbag hook infringed the D'526 design patent under the ordinary observer test, rejecting the argument that it focused on individual details and failed to consider prior art.

13101: No literal infringement by the McGrath Series 5 accused products under the adopted construction

13184: Literal infringement by Tineco's original accused products: the brushroll within the recovery pathway limitation was met.
we see no error in the Commission's finding that Tineco's accused products meet this limitation.

13191: Literal infringement of the locking mechanism limitation of claim 1 of the '043 patent by the 4-in-1 seats; no reasonable jury could find literal infringement.

13195: Literal infringement of the 'backrest' limitation of claim 1 of the '951 patent; substantial evidence supported the jury finding that the accused headrests meet the limitation.

13228: Summary judgment of non-infringement reversed because a reasonable factfinder could find the accused tub has two seating surfaces at differing inclinations and meets the bottom surface limitation.

13229: Denial of TOMY's cross-motion for summary judgment of infringement affirmed because a reasonable factfinder could reject infringement.

13253: Literal infringement: whether accused Simon and Blackhawk point-of-sale systems used unmodified devices meeting every limitation; summary judgment of non-infringement affirmed.

13282: Literal infringement of claim 14 of the '008 patent: jury's noninfringement finding upheld on substantial evidence, after rejecting TQ Delta's argument that a stipulation of standard essentiality compelled infringement.
